00261:head_neck.title: Carboplatin every 3 weeks with head and neck radiotherapy: treatment and checks
00261:head_neck.status: Source reconciled draft; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending
00261:head_neck.setting: Locally advanced stage III–IV head and neck squamous cell carcinoma when cisplatin is not appropriate.
00261:head_neck.summary: Carboplatin is given through a vein over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 21 days. The head and neck prescription uses AUC 5, a target used with your checked kidney function to calculate the dose. The whole visit includes safety checks, anti-sickness medicines, preparation and observation. Three carboplatin cycles are planned with concurrent radiotherapy. Radiation has a separate appointment calendar; the team coordinates any interruptions or changes.

lanes.label: Bloods and organ safety
cells: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests; review kidney-function measurement, earlier platinum reactions, nerve and hearing symptoms and all medicines.
Full blood count, kidney and liver tests before every cycle. The team verifies the current kidney result and dose calculation, and reviews infection, bleeding, hearing and nerve symptoms.
New symptoms may require extra tests before the next planned review.
Safety bloods do not by themselves show whether treatment controls the cancer.

Continue mouth, swallowing, dental, skin and nutrition care after radiation. Blood tests and hearing or nerve review follow any persisting problem; scans and examinations follow your individual oncology and radiation plan.
lanes.note: These stages are not equal time intervals. Your team provides dates and reviews results. There is no universal blood tumour-marker panel or scan interval in this guide.

lanes.label: Concurrent radiotherapy
cells: Dental, nutrition and swallowing preparation; obtain a separate radiation calendar.
Attend radiation on the prescribed calendar; it is not given only on carboplatin days.
Tell the team about missed sessions, skin reactions and worsening mouth or swallowing symptoms.
The radiation and oncology teams coordinate changes.
Recovery and dental or swallowing effects may continue after the final radiation session.
lanes.note: These stages are not equal time intervals. Your team provides dates and reviews results. There is no universal blood tumour-marker panel or scan interval in this guide.

lanes.label: Head and neck function
cells: Record weight, intake, swallowing, speech and existing mouth or dental problems.
Review pain, intake, weight and support needs.
Report choking, inability to drink, worsening swallowing or new neck symptoms.
Agree examinations and scans with the oncology team.
Continue rehabilitation and symptom support as needed.
lanes.note: These stages are not equal time intervals. Your team provides dates and reviews results. There is no universal blood tumour-marker panel or scan interval in this guide.

lanes.label: Medicines and practical plan
cells: Confirm the exact prescription, treatment aim and actual urgent contacts.
Bring your medicine list, current support plan and treatment record.
Record symptoms and medicines taken; ask before adding a new product.
Confirm any pause, dose change or stop in writing.

00483:head_neck.title: Nivolumab every 2 weeks for head and neck cancer: treatment and checks
00483:head_neck.status: Source reconciled draft; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending
00483:head_neck.setting: Recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck after platinum treatment; the cancer cannot be treated with curative local therapy and has progressed or returned within six months of the last platinum dose.
00483:head_neck.summary: Nivolumab is given as 240 mg through a vein over 30 minutes OR 600 mg as an injection under the skin over 3–5 minutes, on Day 1 every 2 weeks. Your team selects one formulation; these doses are not interchangeable milligram for milligram. Allow extra time for safety checks, preparation and observation. Treatment continues until the cancer progresses or side effects become unacceptable, with individual benefit and safety review. There is no fixed number of cycles in this head and neck treatment course.

lanes.label: Bloods and organ safety
cells: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests; review autoimmune disease, transplants, previous immune side effects and all medicines.
Full blood count, kidney and liver tests and glucose before every 2-week cycle. Thyroid tests once a month and when indicated; cortisol when clinically indicated.
New symptoms may require extra tests before the next planned review.
Safety bloods do not by themselves show whether treatment controls the cancer.

Keep reporting new symptoms after treatment ends. Immune side effects require monitoring for at least five months after the last dose. Steroid tapers, hormone replacement or specialist review may continue longer. Scans and examinations follow your individual response and follow-up plan.
lanes.note: These stages are not equal time intervals. Your team provides dates and reviews results. There is no universal blood tumour-marker panel or scan interval in this guide.

lanes.label: Thyroid and other hormones

Thyroid function once a month and when clinically indicated.
New fatigue, dizziness, headache or marked thirst needs review.

Continue hormone follow-up and replacement when prescribed.

00455:head_neck.title: Pembrolizumab every 3 weeks for head and neck cancer: treatment and checks
00455:head_neck.status: Source reconciled draft; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending
00455:head_neck.setting: First-line treatment of metastatic or unresectable recurrent head and neck squamous cell carcinoma with a tumour PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) of at least 1. This indication excludes nasopharyngeal cancer and cancer progressing within six months after curatively intended systemic treatment for locoregionally advanced disease.
00455:head_neck.summary: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given through a vein over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 3 weeks. The whole visit includes safety checks, preparation and observation. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity. After 24 months of sustained response without progression, the team may consider stopping; stopping at 24 months is not automatic.

New symptoms may require extra tests before the next planned review.
Safety bloods do not by themselves show whether treatment controls the cancer.

Keep reporting new symptoms after treatment ends. Steroid tapers, hormone replacement or specialist review may continue longer. Scans and examinations follow your individual response and follow-up plan.
